translation_loss.what_was_lost: The rhythmic and phonetic resonance of the Hindi postpositions 'ka' and 'ki' which establish a musical cadence in the original Devanagari text is flattened in the English prepositional structure.

The literal translation of 'गायों की गिलास' as 'glass of cows' misses the surreal, potentially colloquial, or symbolic nuance of 'gilaas' (glass/tumbler) in relation to cows (perhaps referring to milk or a specific vessel), which sounds highly unusual in English.

original_poem:
सूरज का सातवाँ घोड़ा  
सूरज का सातवाँ घोड़ा,  
रास्ते में आएगा।  
गायों की गिलास लिए,  
किसान की हंसी लिए।  

सूरज का सातवाँ घोड़ा,  
रास्ते में आएगा।  
जो जंग की मूरत है,  
जो हंसता है अमर है।  

गायों की गिलास लिए,  
किसान की हंसी लिए।  
सूरज का सातवाँ घोड़ा,  
रास्ते में आएगा।
translated_poem:
The Seventh Horse of the Sun  
The seventh horse of the sun,  
Will come along the way.  
Carrying the glass of cows,  
Bearing the laughter of farmers.  

The seventh horse of the sun,  
Will come along the way.  
It is the embodiment of war,  
It laughs, it is immortal.  

Carrying the glass of cows,  
Bearing the laughter of farmers.  
The seventh horse of the sun,  
Will come along the way.
